_purpose: Violations of a commercial gate that are ACCEPTED for now, each with an owner, a dated expiry, and the action that clears it.
_why: verify-wbs-chain.py is HARD: an unevidenced completion claim in the Agreed Specification is a contractual statement, so it must fail the gate. But this repository has one such violation TODAY, and a gate that is switched off because reality violates it is the gate-cannot-fail class (x6 in logs/known-failure-modes.md) arriving by the front door. So violations are not waived silently: they are enumerated here, owned, dated, and re-reported as warnings on every run. An exception missing an owner, an action or an expiry FAILS. An expired exception FAILS.
_not_a_waiver: An exception suppresses the FAIL, never the report. Every run still prints the violation with the exception cited against it.

exceptions.gate: verify-flow-definition-language (Secure Outputs on a personal-data read) — NOT a verify-wbs-chain matcher; see _gate_scope_note
exceptions.reason: Six already-shipped ListRecords actions read personal-data rows without runtimeConfiguration.secureData: 2 in REVIntakeWordPressToDataverse (rev_applications, rev_applicants) and 4 in REVScoringDailySummary (rev_applications). Every row either flow reads is therefore recorded in that flow's run history, outside Dataverse's own column security — the exposure C-DOM-004/NFR-012 exists to prevent. Independently re-verified against solution source on 2026-08-25: the count of six is exact. The reviewer risk-accepted it on 2026-08-25, in these words: "Leave the flows for now. It is only run by the service account nobody has access to accept me." The accepted reasoning is that the sole identity running these two flows is the provisioning service account, and the sole person with access to that identity's context is the reviewer, so the population that could ever read the exposed run history is one person who is already entitled to the data. Fixing the six actions is Automation #1 and #2 work and is named by no WBS task, so it is a change-order decision, not something to build first and reconcile later (C-COM-002).
exceptions.clears_when: Two steps, in order, and the first does not yet exist. (1) The Secure-Outputs check must be BUILT into scripts/verify-flow-definition-language.py — IMP-0320 describes it as 'check 5' already added in that dispatch, and it is not on disk: the script is unmodified against HEAD, declares three checks rather than the four IMP-0320 credits it with, and the string 'secureData' appears nowhere in scripts/ (re-verified 2026-08-25, recorded as IMP-0322). (2) A change order adds runtimeConfiguration.secureData to the six named actions, after which that check is wired into config/revitalise-grant-automation-build.yml as a HARD step for the whole solution. Until step 1 lands, no gate anywhere can observe this gap, so this exception is the only record of it — which is why its expiry is the control that matters.
exceptions.expiry_rationale: The two flows are Automation #1 and Automation #2, which contract/service-agreement.json maps to agreement phase_1 and phase_2; the later of their two milestones is the date by which both automations are due, so the exception cannot outlive the phases that own the flows. Deliberately NOT the 2026-11-27 date EX-001 and EX-003 use: the reviewer's accepted reasoning rests on the premise that one trusted person holds the only access, and the moment most likely to break that premise — a second environment administrator, a flow owner other than the service account, or production handover — arrives after these phases close, so the exception must be re-decided before then rather than ride to go-live.
exceptions._risk_acceptance_note: This is a risk acceptance, not a finding that the exposure is harmless. If a second identity gains flow-owner or environment-administrator access to the environment running these flows, the premise fails and this exception must be re-decided immediately, ahead of its expiry.

The reviewer (Xander Lykopoulos) directed proceeding to build and display the ethnic-group distribution now, in DEV, ahead of that sign-off, on 2026-08-31, in these words: "Ethnic group is on the applicant table right now. Until then the ethnic-group chart is DEV-only, consistent with the trustee portal's existing EX-003 boundary.

exceptions._risk_acceptance_note: This is a risk acceptance of proceeding ahead of formal DPIA sign-off, not a finding that the sign-off is unnecessary. OQ-030 stays open and must still close before this feature (or this chart specifically) reaches TST/ACC or PRD.

_gate_scope_note: EX-004 is the first entry here for a TECHNOLOGY gate rather than a commercial one, and C-COM-010's wording ('an accepted violation of a commercial gate') has not been widened to match. It is recorded here because IMP-0320's own proposed_change named this file and the reviewer directed option (b) of it by name. Mechanically it is enforced exactly like the others — verify-wbs-chain.py validates every entry's owner, clearing action and expiry regardless of which gate it names, and fails on an unowned or expired one — but its 'matches' string will never fire against a verify-wbs-chain message, so the expiry is what carries it. Whether C-COM-010 should be widened, or technology exceptions given their own home, is an open altitude call for the next improvement review (pm-agent owns C-COM-010).
_no_v06_note: Both exceptions originally cleared via a WBS v0.6 re-approval. The reviewer confirmed on 2026-08-19 that no v0.6 will be issued. An exception whose clearing action can never happen is a permanent waiver, which C-COM-010 exists to prevent — so both were re-homed onto actions that are actually available.
